chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:
We order our children to perform Salat when they are five years old, so you should order your children to perform Salat when they are seven years old.

And we order our children to fast when they are seven years old, with whatever they can bear from fasting the day, whether it is up to half the day, or more than that, or less. So when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they become accustomed to fasting and are able to endure it.
So order your children to fast when they are nine years old, for whatever they can bear of fasting the day. So when thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.
ai.seo_question: At what age should children start praying and fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the pedagogical framework for *Tadrib* (training) rather than immediate obligation, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus that pre-pubertal children are not yet bound by *Taklif*. It highlights a gradualist approach where prayer instruction begins at age five to build habit, while fasting is introduced at age seven with flexibility for physical limits, culminating in full-day fasting expectations by age nine.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Weasws tend to order ourasws children with the Salāt when they are five years of age, therefore, instruct your children with the Salāt when they were seven years of age.

And we<sup>asws</sup> tend to order our<sup>asws</sup> children with the Fasting when they were of seven years with whatever they can bear from the Fasting of the day. If it was up to half the day, or more than that, or less. So when the thirst and the hunger overcomes them, they break, until they become habitual with the Fasting and are able to endure it.
Therefore, instruct you children when they were of seven years, with the Fasting, whatever they capacities may be, from the Fasting of the day. So when the thirst overcomes them, they break it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
We instruct our children to perform Salah (prayer) when they are five years old. Instruct your children to perform Salah (prayer) when they are seven years old.

We instruct our children to fast when they are seven years old if they can endure fasting even up to midday, or more than this or less. When thirst bothers them and hunger they discontinue the fast. This is to familiarize them with fasting to build their endurance to fast.
So instruct your children to fast when they are nine years old and for as much of the day they can fast. When thirst bothers them, then you should allow them to discontinue their fast.’”
